Question B-007-001-007.

Why the correct answer is right: At lower HF in daylight, ground wave can provide comparatively local to regional coverage when sky-wave conditions may not fill that range.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Tropospheric ducting": Tropospheric ducting is an enhanced VHF/UHF-style lower-atmosphere effect, not the ordinary lower-HF daytime mechanism in this distance range.
- sourceIndex 2: "Skip wave": Skip wave would involve an ionospheric return; the stated lower-HF daytime local range is being credited to surface-guided energy.
- sourceIndex 3: "Space wave": Space wave is a line-of-sight family of paths and does not explain this lower-HF surface-following coverage.
